summary.text: Cell division is the process by which a parent cell divides into two daughter cells.
In eukaryotes there are two types: mitosis, which makes daughter cells genetically identical to the parent, and meiosis, which makes haploid gametes for sexual reproduction.
All cell divisions, whatever the organism, are preceded by a single round of DNA replication.

facts.label: Mitosis outcome
facts.value: Genetically identical cells, with chromosome number maintained

facts.label: Meiosis outcome
facts.value: Two divisions give four haploid daughter cells

facts.label: Prokaryote method
facts.value: Usually binary fission, splitting genetic material equally

facts.label: Lifetime divisions
facts.value: The human body has about 10 quadrillion

facts.label: Single-celled organisms
facts.value: For an amoeba, one division equals reproduction

items.prompt: A gardener plants a cutting, and it grows into a whole new plant. Which kind of cell division makes this possible?

options.label: Mitosis, which produces genetically identical cells
Meiosis, which produces haploid gametes
Binary fission, which is how bacteria divide
Amitosis, a primitive form of cell division

items.explain: Mitotic cell division can create progeny from multicellular organisms, such as plants that grow from cuttings.

items.prompt: Egg and sperm cells must each carry half the usual set of chromosomes. Which division makes cells like that?

options.label: Mitosis, which keeps the chromosome number the same
Binary fission, which splits genetic material equally
Meiosis, which reduces the chromosome number
Amitosis, a primitive form of cell division

items.explain: Meiosis produces haploid gametes by reducing the chromosomes from two of each type to one of each type.

items.prompt: A person begins as a single cell formed when two gametes fuse. What lets that one cell grow into a whole body?

options.label: Meiosis, repeated until enough cells exist
Binary fission, as in bacteria
Amitosis, a primitive form of cell division
Mitosis, which builds and repairs the organism

items.explain: Mitotic cell division lets sexually reproducing organisms develop from the one-celled zygote and then allows continual construction and repair.

items.prompt: A single bacterium makes two new cells from itself. Which method does it usually use?

options.label: Mitosis, with chromosomes lining up on a plate
Binary fission, splitting its genetic material equally
Meiosis, halving its chromosomes first
Gametic meiosis, producing four gametes

items.explain: Prokaryotes such as bacteria usually divide by binary fission, segregating their genetic material equally into two daughter cells.

items.prompt: An amoeba divides, and a whole new organism exists. What is different about cell division inside the body of a grown animal?

options.label: It repairs or adds to the existing organism rather than making a new one
It always produces haploid gametes instead of ordinary cells
It happens without any DNA replication beforehand
It cuts the chromosome number in half every time

items.explain: For a simple single-celled organism one division is reproduction, but in an adult mitosis allows continual construction and repair of the organism.

items.prompt: A cell's DNA is damaged as it moves through the cell cycle. What can the checkpoints do?

options.label: Rush the cell through so it divides before the damage spreads
Copy the damaged DNA twice so that one good copy survives
Halt progress through the cycle while the damage is repaired
Skip DNA replication and go straight to the division

items.explain: DNA damage is detected and repaired at cell cycle checkpoints, which can halt progression through the cycle.
